title: Obstruction to adjunction laws for arbitrary right comparisons
statement: Fix a prime l, an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l, a finite-field datum D with l ≠ D.p, finite-type schemes X,Y over D.k, a separated finite-type relative morphism f:X→Y, a compactification c, operation and compact-support left-realization families, and a transport datum d as defined in [lem-sf-exceptional-ring-transport-core-data]. If at a stage E the supplied right comparison differs from the canonical comparison in [lem-sf-exceptional-system-adjunction-normalized-comparison], the displayed adjunction equality fails. More generally let α_E be a natural automorphism of the integral operation right functor at every stage, with α_E0 not the identity at some stage E0. There cannot be an adjunction comparison law for every transport datum with the same parameters: the datum obtained by changing realizeG_E to α_E followed by the canonical comparison has no such law. In particular the conclusion holds if, for some integral object K at Y and stage E, minus the identity of A_E.G(K) differs from its identity; take α_E to be the negative identity natural automorphism at all stages. These negations explicitly assume the nonidentity automorphism or component; they do not assert it exists on a zero category.

proof.text: The pointwise necessary and sufficient condition for the adjunction equation immediately excludes a noncanonical supplied comparison.

Update only realizeG_E to α_E followed by the canonical comparison. This remains a valid TransportCoreData because no other field depends on realizeG. A universal law applied to this update and the uniqueness condition would give α_E0 followed by e_E0 equals e_E0. Compose both sides on the right with e_E0 inverse; associativity and the two inverse identities force α_E0 to be the identity, contradicting the hypothesis.

Each integral category is preadditive, so negation of the identity natural isomorphism is again a natural automorphism of each right functor. If it were the identity at E, equality of its component at K would contradict the specified minus-identity inequality. Apply the preceding twist obstruction. At the identity twist the canonical law remains true; on a zero category the nonidentity hypothesis is unavailable.
